Subject: Recap + next steps: Redwood vs hyperscaler TCO & benchmark plan

Hi Sophie / Rajiv - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap
- Primary goals: lower inference cost for your conversational flows (customer support + recommendations) and reduce 99th pctl latency for realtime responses.
- Key constraints: must remain within FinPay's PCI-adjacent controls, prefer dedicated deployment for production if unit economics justify it.
- Evaluation asks you mentioned: per-1M token TCO, impact of batching and cache on unit costs, and an apples-to-apples latency comparison vs Hyperscaler A's managed endpoint.

Redwood differentiators (short)
- Production-first runtime with continuous batching + KV prefix caching (helps reduce effective tokens served).
- Clear unit economics and predictable reserved pricing (Dedicated) to drive down per-token costs.
- Smart routing + fallbacks to keep SLAs without manual ops.

Proposed next steps
1) Shared benchmark run: we'll run a short 2k-request benchmark that mirrors your distribution (avg request ~120 tokens, prompt prefix ~40 tokens) and replicate typical batching (you said batch sizes around 8). We'll compare Redwood hosted, Redwood Dedicated (small committed pool), and Hyperscaler A managed endpoint.
2) I've attached a TCO model and a benchmark playbook (redwood_tco_model.xlsx, benchmark-instructions.md). Please fill the simple tab in the spreadsheet with your monthly QPS and any reserved-commit preferences so we can run the committed capacity scenario.
3) Marcus will pull together back-of-envelope per-1M token numbers (hosted vs hyperscaler vs dedicated) with different cache-hit assumptions.
4) Schedule the benchmark for next week if that works for you - we can run it in a non-prod VPC and share raw logs + summary.

Questions for you (so we can size accurately)
- Confirm typical batch size (you mentioned 8; is that fixed?),
- Approx distribution of request length (p50/p90),
- Expected KV/prefix cache hit rate (estimates are fine).

If you confirm, I'll get Marcus to draft the initial per-1M token TCO table and set up the benchmark plan.

Thanks - Aditya

Thanks Sophie - adding some concrete numbers and assumptions below (back-of-envelope). I've attached a short PDF with the same numbers and the model tabs in the spreadsheet.

Assumptions (baseline)
- Avg tokens/request (prompt + output): 160
- Batch size: 8
- KV cache hit rate: 25% baseline (we'll show 0/15/25/40% in the model)
- Benchmark traffic shape: 80% short (<=200 tokens), 20% long (>200 tokens)

Rough per-1M token costs (effective tokens served after cache)
- Redwood hosted (multi-tenant): $7.50 / 1M tokens @ 25% cache hit (includes runtime + infra overhead)
- Hyperscaler A managed: $12.40 / 1M tokens (their published model price + network infra)
- Redwood Dedicated (10k t/s committed pool): $4.20 / 1M tokens equivalent (committed discount + packing)

Notes on calculation
- Effective tokens = nominal_tokens * (1 - cache_hit_rate). For 25% hit on 160 tokens/request -> effective 120 tokens/request.
- Batching improves throughput and reduces per-token GPU overhead; our model assumes continuous batching at target batch size across the request mix.
- Latency: with batch size 8 our p95 is typically in the 80-110ms range on comparable GPU configs; Hyperscaler's 120ms p95 is in the same ballpark but their tail can be more variable under mixed workloads. The benchmark will produce p50/p95/p99 histograms.

Suggested benchmark window
- Wed 24 Jun (early slot) or Thu 25 Jun. We'll need ~2 hours of stable traffic to get meaningful stats. We'll run three variants: Redwood hosted, Redwood dedicated (small pool), Hyperscaler A endpoint (we'll simulate using their public endpoint).

Next steps / asks
- Sophie/Rajiv: confirm Wed/Thu preference and provide a procurement contact if you want us to include a committed pricing quote (Marcus/Marissa can draft).
- Sophie: if you can drop rough monthly QPS into the spreadsheet we'll finalize committed sizing and cost math.

I'll follow with the populated redwood_tco_model.xlsx and the benchmark checklist shortly.

Thanks - Marcus
